subject: Draft MAP: technical evaluation playbook & target acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Emily Ross <emily.ross@healthcomp.io>, Michael Stein <michael.stein@healthcomp.io>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T15:22:00Z
Subject: Draft MAP: technical evaluation playbook & target acceptance criteria

Hi Emily / Michael —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I attached a first-pass MAP focused on the technical evaluation milestone so we have a clear owner/responsibility split and measurable acceptance criteria. High-level summary below. The attached spreadsheet (HC_MAP_draft_v1.xlsx) contains the milestone rows you can pull into your procurement/IT tracker.

Quick summary of the technical-eval milestone (recommended):
- Objective: Validate Redwood inference performance and cost for HealthComp’s triage+summarization workload on representative data.
- Success criteria (pass/fail):
  - Latency: median p95 generation latency <= 180ms for 512-token prompt under 8 concurrent sessions (on our Dedicated config).
  - Cost: steady-state per-1000-token inference cost under $X.XX when using recommended quantization and batching profile (see template).
  - Accuracy/quality: pass rate >= 92% on the provided eval prompt set (we’ll run blind scoring + provide examples).
- Model shortlist to test: Llama-3-70B-ct-8q (quantized), Mistral-Instruct-65B, and Redwood-Base-30B (quantized) — we can add your preferred vendor models if you share them.
- Test plan owner: Redwood (Monica) to run benchmarks; HealthComp to provide sample prompt set + 3 production request traces, redacted.
- Target completion: 3 weeks from kickoff (tentative close milestone in MAP: 2026-09-19).
- Dependencies: data handoff (sample prompts/traces), network access for dedicated nodes (if you choose Dedicated), and procurement signoff for limited test access.

Next steps I propose:
1) Emily/Michael: confirm the acceptance criteria above and add any SLA/region constraints.
2) HealthComp: upload the sample prompt set + two redacted request traces to the Drive link and confirm preferred test models (deadline: 2026-09-02).
3) Redwood: Monica will provision a bench, run the test matrix, and share raw results + a summary report.

I’ve included the benchmark template (redwood_benchmark_template.csv) in the attachments. Lauren — FYI for pricing/commit notes to include in the MAP. Monica — can you confirm bench availability for the proposed window?

Thanks,
Priyom
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
pri...@redwood.com
(attachment: HC_MAP_draft_v1.xlsx, redwood_benchmark_template.csv)

From: Emily Ross <emily.ross@healthcomp.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Stein <michael.stein@healthcomp.io>
Date: 2026-08-30T10:11:00Z
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: technical evaluation playbook & target acceptance criteria

Priyom —

Thanks for the concise summary and the draft MAP. A few clarifications from our side before we sign off on the milestone: 

1) Latency: the 180ms p95 target looks aggressive but reasonable as a goal; can you confirm whether that number assumes GPU warm-cache and whether it includes network egress between our VPC and Redwood Dedicated? We may need a network SLO carve-out.
2) Cost: please replace the placeholder cost figure with a projected per-1000-token cost estimate for both hosted and dedicated scenarios so procurement can weigh options.
3) Models: we’d like to add Anthropic-Inst-70b as an optional candidate for the evaluation matrix (if Redwood supports it).
4) Data handoff: we can provide the prompt set by 2026-09-03 (not 09-02) — procurement will need the extra business day.

Also, who from our side will be the technical contact for Redis/network testing? I’ll carbon-copy them once we confirm the window.

Best,
Emily Ross
CTO, HealthComp
(emily.ross@healthcomp.io)

Thanks Emily — great questions. Quick replies inline: 

- Latency scope: the 180ms p95 is measured end-to-end from request arrival at the Redwood edge to token generation completion on the selected Dedicated instance with warm KV cache. We will annotate results with and without network hop to your VPC. If you require a network SLO carve-out, we’ll mark the MAP milestone accordingly.
- Cost estimates: Lauren, can you attach a short worksheet with hosted vs dedicated projected per-1k-token rates based on the load profile Emily shared? Lauren, suggest we include a conservative and an optimized estimate (quantized + batching).
- Anthropic-Inst-70b: we can add it to the matrix as an optional run — Monica, please include Anthropic in the bench queue if supported by the infra.
- Data handoff: updated deadline noted (2026-09-03) — that’s fine.

Monica — can you confirm bench availability the week of 09/06 and whether we need any additional network work from HealthComp to run the Dedicated scenario? If Anthropic requires a separate runtime, note that in the bench plan.

Emily/Michael — after Monica confirms capacity, I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff to align on test cadence and scoring rubric.

Regards,
Priyom

Subject: Re: Draft MAP: technical evaluation playbook & target acceptance criteria

Priyom / team —

I’ve reserved bench capacity the week of 2026-09-06 for the initial runs. Plan:
- Day 1: smoke tests + environment validation (5 hours)
- Day 2-4: run full matrix for three models (scheduled batches, 6–8 hour windows)
- Day 5: aggregate results, generate pass/fail report and short readout deck.

Anthropic-Inst-70b: infra supports Anthropic via our marketplace connector; add ~4 hours to setup and an extra cost line (I'll document).

Network: for Dedicated end-to-end tests we’ll need a temporary peering/VPN and a small NAT egress rule to allow metric upload. Emily — if HealthComp can provision the VPC peering request by 2026-09-04, we’ll include the Dedicated runs in the same window.

Deliverables and owners (to add to the MAP row):
- Bench execution and raw logs: Monica (Redwood)
- Results summary & slide readout: Monica + Priyom (Redwood)
- Cost worksheet (hosted vs dedicated): Lauren (Redwood)
- Security/approval notes: HealthComp security contact (tbd)

I’ll upload the initial raw results and readout to the Drive folder and ping when ready.

—Monica
